topStories.headline: Community Rallies Save Richmond Neighborhood Center — For Now
topStories.dek: SFUSD quietly shelved a developer solicitation for the Outer Richmond site after more than 100 residents stormed a school board meeting, but the nonprofit's lease still expires in June 2027.
topStories.body:
The Richmond Neighborhood Center won a hard-fought reprieve this week after a swift community campaign forced the San Francisco Unified School District to pull back a plan that could have displaced the Outer Richmond nonprofit from its longtime home. Directors at the center learned in August that SFUSD, which owns the land at 741 30th Ave., planned to begin soliciting developers in September to gauge redevelopment costs — a process that would have put the site on a path toward housing construction. Word spread fast.

On the evening of September 8, more than 100 people packed the SFUSD Board of Education meeting after rallying outside district headquarters, demanding a transparent public process before any decision was made about the property, which has housed the Richmond Neighborhood Center since 1980. Staff had been notified that the request for proposals would go out the very next day. It ultimately did not, following an intense wave of social media posts, emails, calls, and letters to board members and elected officials.

The district confirmed the reversal in writing. "We can confirm that the property that Richmond District Neighborhood Center is leasing is not on the upcoming [request for proposals]," a district spokesperson wrote, as reported by the Richmond Review. The school district said in a statement on Tuesday, September 9, that there are no current plans to redevelop the 741 30th Ave. property.

But center leaders were careful not to declare victory. The nonprofit's lease is set to expire on June 30, 2027, and the underlying question — what SFUSD intends to do with the land long-term — remains unresolved. The organization serves more than 6,000 youth, families, and seniors and partners with 12 SFUSD schools. Supporters note that Richmond residents fought off a similar redevelopment threat 46 years ago and kept the site as community space. The fight, for now, is paused — not over.

topStories.headline: The Presidio's 250th Birthday Arrives Thursday
topStories.dek: September 17 marks 250 years to the day since El Presidio de San Francisco was founded, with public screenings of a new documentary at the Presidio Chapel commemorating the milestone.
topStories.body:
The week that residents and history enthusiasts have been anticipating all year is finally here. Thursday, September 17, 2026 marks the precise 250th anniversary of the founding of El Presidio de San Francisco — the Spanish colonial garrison established on September 17, 1776, that gave rise to the park, the military post, and ultimately the city that surrounds it.

The Presidio Historical Association is anchoring the day's commemoration at the Presidio Chapel, 130 Fisher Loop, with public showings at 1 p.m., 2 p.m., and 3 p.m. of a completed audio-visual documentary on the Anza expedition — the overland journey from Sonora, Mexico, that brought the founding settlers to the bay. Filmmaker Luis Valle completed a bicycle re-enactment of the entire Anza route earlier this year, arriving at Fort Point in March, and the film that grew from that journey makes its full public debut on the anniversary.

The Presidio's story spans far longer than 250 years: the Ramaytush Ohlone people lived on this land for thousands of years before Spanish colonists arrived, and the site subsequently passed through Mexican and U.S. Army control before becoming one of America's most visited national park sites. As the country marks the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence this year, the Presidio offers what its stewards describe as a rare window into the parallel, often overlooked history of the West Coast in 1776.

The Presidio Trust, the National Park Service, and the Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy have coordinated anniversary programming throughout 2026. Visitors can also explore self-guided walks, Battery Bluff, El Polín Spring, and free exhibitions at the Presidio Officers' Club and Presidio Visitor Center throughout the anniversary period. Admission to the chapel commemoration is free.

topStories.headline: Geary Dig Nears the Finish Line Underground — Street-Level Work Is Next
topStories.dek: The SFPUC's Geary Boulevard sewer and water project hit 80 percent completion, and SFMTA is now preparing to begin the surface improvements — bus bulbs, new paving, and pedestrian upgrades — this fall.
topStories.body:
The years-long infrastructure overhaul beneath Geary Boulevard is entering its final underground chapter, and the above-ground phase that will reshape the corridor for transit riders and pedestrians is coming into view. The San Francisco Public Utilities Commission reported as of August 10 that the Phase 2 sewer and water replacement project is more than 80 percent complete and remains ahead of schedule.

Work in Segment A — from 32nd Avenue toward the inner avenues — is 100 percent done. In Segment B, stretching from 12th Avenue toward Stanyan Street, all sewer, water, and fiber installation has been completed, and crews are now focused on restoring parking strips, curbs, gutters, and roadways. Temporary paving is in place until final street restoration begins under a separate project. The full underground project is on track for completion in spring 2027.

The visible phase is the one that will change daily life on Geary most noticeably. SFMTA is preparing to begin its own construction this fall, adding bus and pedestrian curb extensions, upgrading traffic signals, completing full roadway paving, and installing neighborhood enhancements — including new trees and decorative sidewalk designs chosen through a community input process. The agency's surface work is planned to run from late 2026 through late 2027.

For riders of the 38 Geary and 38R Geary Rapid, some bus stops remain temporarily relocated during active construction zones; SFMTA advises riders to look for orange signage at affected stops. The $50 million project replaces water and sewer infrastructure that dates to the late 1800s, and is intended to provide reliable service to Richmond District homes and businesses for the next century.

moreNews.headline: Loaded Ghost Gun Found in Robotaxi During Predawn Outer Richmond Stop
moreNews.body: San Francisco police conducted a high-risk traffic stop on an autonomous vehicle in the Outer Richmond in the early hours of September 3, after receiving a report that two passengers inside the vehicle had a firearm. Officers responded to the 800 block of 40th Avenue at approximately 3:52 a.m. and detained both passengers. A search of the vehicle turned up a loaded AR-style ghost gun — an untraceable weapon assembled from unserialized parts — along with suspected marijuana and mace spray. Both passengers, identified as juveniles, were arrested on charges related to illegal possession of a firearm and booked accordingly, according to the San Francisco Police Department. The case remains active. The arrest was reported by Hoodline on September 11.

moreNews.headline: Kitchen Commons Cookware Shop Coming to Clement Street This Fall
moreNews.body: A new neighborhood shop for home cooks is taking shape at 130 Clement St., the Inner Richmond address previously occupied by the Spanish Table, which closed late last year. Jeff Hanak, a partner at Liholiho Yacht Club, Good Good Culture Club, and Nopalito, and Connor Bruce, a former Nopalito employee, plan to open Kitchen Commons this fall. The store will stock new and vintage cookware, pantry staples, cookbooks, and local ceramics, and will include a small café serving coffee and prepared foods. The owners, both longtime Inner Richmond residents, also envision the space as a community hub, with regular cooking classes, talks, and events. No specific opening date had been announced as of the SF Standard's May 7 report.

Clement Street's next food destination isn't a restaurant

restaurants.name: Rose Pizzeria
restaurants.description: Berkeley's nationally acclaimed thin-crust pizzeria, named one of America's best by the New York Times, opened its first San Francisco location on the prominent Clement and Arguello corner in 2026.

restaurants.name: Chapeau!
restaurants.description: Beloved family-run French bistro from chef-owner Philippe Gardelle serving classic escargots, coq au vin, and prix-fixe menus in a cozy Clement Street setting since 1996.

restaurants.name: Burma Superstar
restaurants.description: Iconic Burmese restaurant famous for its tea leaf salad and rainbow salad, drawing lines down Clement Street for decades.

restaurants.name: B Star
restaurants.description: Sister restaurant to Burma Superstar offering a more casual, bar-forward experience with many of the same beloved Burmese flavors plus cocktails.

restaurants.name: Arsicault Bakery
restaurants.description: Bon Appétit's best new bakery in America when it opened in 2015, Arsicault draws weekend lines stretching down Arguello for its supremely flaky croissants, kouign amann, and morning buns.

restaurants.name: Dalida
restaurants.description: Acclaimed restaurant from chef couple Laura and Sayat Ozyilmaz set on the Presidio's Main Parade Lawn, celebrated for its pillowy pita, tahdig, and Cypriot lamb chops with sweeping Alcatraz views.

restaurants.name: Maria Isabel
restaurants.description: Upscale Mexican restaurant from the Dalida team, drawing on chef Laura Ozyilmaz's Guerrero coastal upbringing with dishes like ceviche acapulqueño, sourdough tortillas, and seasonal California-sourced ingredients.

restaurants.name: Cinderella Russian Bakery
restaurants.description: A Richmond institution since 1953 serving piroshki, borscht, pelmeni, and Eastern European pastries to generations of neighborhood regulars.

restaurants.name: Mandalay Restaurant
restaurants.description: Long-standing Burmese restaurant on California Street celebrated for its ginger salad, mohinga fish noodle soup, and warm family-run hospitality.

restaurants.name: Kitchen Istanbul
restaurants.description: Intimate Clement Street restaurant offering Turkish and Eastern Mediterranean dishes including mezze, kebabs, and housemade baklava in a warmly decorated space.

restaurants.name: Pizzetta 211
restaurants.description: Tiny, reservation-free Outer Richmond spot turning out small-batch, seasonal thin-crust pizzas with a rotating menu of just a few options, beloved for its simplicity and quality.

restaurants.name: Mess Hall at Presidio Tunnel Tops
restaurants.description: The Presidio's newest dining destination, an all-day food hall adjacent to Tunnel Tops featuring a café serving Wrecking Ball Coffee, a full cocktail bar, three food concepts, and a retail market in a historic building with San Francisco Bay views.

restaurants.name: Pacific Café
restaurants.description: A 51-year-old Richmond institution at the corner of Geary and 34th Avenue, serving fresh seafood plates with Boudin sourdough and offering every waiting guest a complimentary glass of wine — a tradition since 1974.

restaurants.name: Plough and Stars
restaurants.description: Beloved Irish pub on Clement Street with live traditional music sessions most nights of the week and a warm neighborhood atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Richmond Republic Draught House
restaurants.description: Lively Clement Street craft beer bar with a rotating lineup of local and regional taps, a relaxed vibe, and a neighborhood gathering-spot feel.

restaurants.name: Toy Boat Dessert Café
restaurants.description: Charming dessert café filled with vintage tin toys, serving scoops of Clover ice cream, sodas, and espresso drinks to families and neighbors since 1979.

restaurants.name: Trad'r Sam
restaurants.description: Old-school Outer Richmond tiki bar open since 1937, serving strong, colorful cocktails in a kitschy, low-lit room beloved for its no-frills, time-warp atmosphere.

hotels.name: Inn at the Presidio
hotels.description: A 22-room historic boutique hotel inside the Presidio, set in a restored Georgian Revival officers' building with complimentary continental breakfast, afternoon wine and cheese receptions, and fire-pit porches with Golden Gate views.

hotels.name: Lodge at the Presidio
hotels.description: A second Presidio Trust boutique hotel in a historic building on the Main Post, offering European-style breakfast buffets, afternoon wine and cheese, and a serene national park setting steps from Crissy Field.

shops.name: Green Apple Books & Music
shops.description: Beloved Richmond independent bookstore since 1967, with two Clement Street locations packed floor-to-ceiling with new and used books, music, and film; in 2026, the Sunset location opened its upstairs as a literary co-working space.

shops.name: Clement Street Farmers Market
shops.description: Year-round Sunday farmers market across three blocks of Clement Street in the Inner Richmond, featuring organic produce, baked goods, flowers, and specialty vendors from across the Bay Area.

shops.name: Sports Basement Presidio
shops.description: Large, well-priced outdoor and sporting goods retailer in the Presidio's historic Thoreau Center, carrying gear for hiking, cycling, camping, and watersports alongside apparel and rentals.

shops.name: Aroma Tea Shop
shops.description: Specialty tea shop on Clement Street with a vast selection of loose-leaf teas from China and Taiwan, teaware, and knowledgeable staff who guide customers through brewing techniques.

shops.name: Dragon's Gate Art
shops.description: Clement Street gallery and gift shop specializing in Asian art, ceramics, silk, and unique home goods sourced from across East and Southeast Asia.

shops.name: Lakeshore Natural Foods
shops.description: Community-focused natural foods market on California Street carrying organic produce, bulk goods, supplements, and specialty items for health-conscious Richmond shoppers.

shops.name: Park Life
shops.description: Celebrated Inner Richmond shop and small-press gallery combining design books, zines, art prints, and curated objects by local and international artists.

shops.name: Sloat Garden Center
shops.description: Full-service garden center on Geary Boulevard carrying a wide range of plants, soils, tools, and gardening supplies for Richmond residents and Golden Gate Park-adjacent gardeners.

artEntertainment.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
artEntertainment.description: Forty-thousand-square-foot non-profit museum in the Presidio dedicated to the life and legacy of Walt Disney, with ten interactive galleries, over 200 video screens, early animations, personal artifacts, and a spectacular scale model of Disneyland.

artEntertainment.name: Legion of Honor
artEntertainment.description: Landmark fine arts museum in Lincoln Park at the edge of the Richmond, housing a permanent collection spanning 4,000 years of art alongside world-class traveling exhibitions including the current Etruscans show through September 20.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Theatre
artEntertainment.description: Restored 600-seat theater on the Presidio's Main Post hosting film screenings, live performances, community events, and — on September 17 — the world premiere of the Anza 250 documentary marking the park's 250th birthday.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Officers' Club
artEntertainment.description: Historic adobe building on the Presidio's Main Post housing free exhibitions including the ongoing EXCLUSION show on the WWII Japanese American incarceration, plus the Heritage Gallery tracing the park's 250-year history.

artEntertainment.name: ArtSeed at Tides Converge
artEntertainment.description: Presidio-based arts education nonprofit hosting free exhibitions in the China Brotsky and Seed Galleries, including the current 20th Annual Open Call Exhibition, 'So What Now?', running through September 18.

artEntertainment.name: Plough and Stars
artEntertainment.description: Clement Street Irish pub and live music institution hosting traditional music sessions most nights, making it one of the best spots in San Francisco for authentic acoustic Irish folk and trad.

artEntertainment.name: 4 Star Theater
artEntertainment.description: Independent cinema on Clement Street showing a mix of current releases, art house films, and free family-friendly weekend morning screenings in 2026.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Visitor Center
artEntertainment.type: National park visitor center and gallery
artEntertainment.description: The Presidio Trust's main visitor center offers free self-guided and ranger-led programming, rotating interpretive exhibitions, and serves as the starting point for exploring the park's 250 years of layered history.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Golf Course
gymsRecreation.description: Historic public golf course in the Presidio, one of the most scenic on the West Coast, with fairways winding through cypress and eucalyptus groves with views of the Golden Gate Bridge.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Bowling Center
gymsRecreation.description: Twelve-lane bowling alley in the Presidio with a full grill menu, a selection of 45 beers and ciders, and open lanes for drop-in bowling, private events, and league play.

gymsRecreation.name: Rob Hill Campground
gymsRecreation.description: One of only two campgrounds in San Francisco, Rob Hill Campground in the Presidio is open April through October and bookable through recreation.gov, offering a true urban camping experience minutes from the city.
gymsRecreation.address: Washington Blvd at Immigrant Point Trail, Presidio

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Tunnel Tops
gymsRecreation.description: Expansive park above the Presidio Parkway tunnels with sweeping Golden Gate Bridge views, a campfire circle, playground, and event meadows hosting free community programs throughout summer.

gymsRecreation.name: Crissy Field
gymsRecreation.type: Restored tidal marsh and beachfront park
gymsRecreation.description: Iconic restored wetlands and beach along the Presidio waterfront offering walking and cycling on the Golden Gate Promenade, kite flying, windsurfing, and Golden Gate Bridge views.

gymsRecreation.name: Sports Basement Presidio — Rentals & Fitness
gymsRecreation.type: Outdoor gear rental and fitness events
gymsRecreation.description: The Presidio Sports Basement location hosts regular demo runs, fitness events, and rents bikes, camping, and outdoor gear, making it a hub for active Presidio visitors.

gymsRecreation.name: Mountain Lake Park
gymsRecreation.description: Peaceful park in the Inner Richmond/Lake Street neighborhood surrounding one of San Francisco's only remaining natural lakes, with a playground, walking paths, and restored wetland habitat.

gymsRecreation.name: Lincoln Park
gymsRecreation.description: Rugged headlands park in the Outer Richmond home to the Legion of Honor museum, the Land's End coastal trail with dramatic ocean and Golden Gate views, and the historic Sutro Baths ruins.

gymsRecreation.name: Ocean Beach
gymsRecreation.description: Three-mile stretch of Pacific Ocean beach bordering the Outer Richmond, popular for surfing, walking, bonfires in designated fire rings, and dramatic sunsets over the water.
